product_intent: A private reading and research room over the 257 books The Holy Word gathered, kept open in memory of Joe Felz. It must let one person read a scanned page beside its transcription, search by word and by meaning, follow names across books, and see where every line came from.
audience: Joe's friends and the owner of this archive: people who knew him or his work, reading alone on one Windows computer, usually for a long sitting. Not researchers on a deadline, not the public.
emotional_objective: Quiet, sunlit attention. The feeling of being let into a private library by someone who loved the books, with the man remembered in the room's light rather than in a banner.
creative_thesis: By day the cell gathers; by night the lamp gives back. Joe wired solar panels and photographed old books: both are the act of catching light. The room is lit by the reader's own sun: its ground, ink and accent follow the local hour, and Joe's two colours trade places as the sun goes. Solar-cell blue is the ink of the day and gilt is the lamp of the night. Everything else is set as the books themselves were set: a title page, a contents leaf, running heads, side-notes, an index with leaders, a colophon.
anti_generic_risk: Dark navy and gold reads as stock 'luxury dark mode'. Countered by making darkness one of five states of a clock-driven light, and by giving day the primary role.
Parchment skeuomorphism (stained paper, torn edges, fake leather). Refused: paper is flat, clean and lit; age comes only from the real scans.
Dashboard cards, pills and icon circles. Refused: there are no cards. Structure is carried by rules, leaders, columns and type, as in a printed book.
Knowledge-graph spaghetti with neon nodes. The names chart is drawn as an engraved star chart with magnitudes and says plainly that it shows shared pages, not relationships.

style_world_dna.typography: IM Fell types (Igino Marini's digitisations of the 17th-century Fell types) for titles and display, because a third of this library was printed in faces like them; EB Garamond for reading and for all interface text, with letterspaced small capitals for labels and old-style figures throughout. Monospace appears only for hashes and engine names.
style_world_dna.structure: The ruling. Manuscripts were pricked and ruled before a word was written; a solar cell is a field ruled by silver busbars. Hairline rules, double rules and dot leaders are the only containers.
style_world_dna.light: Five keyed palettes (dawn, noon, golden hour, dusk, night) blended by the local clock in OKLab. Light phases put ink on sunlit plaster; dark phases put lamplight on cell blue. Scanned pages are always the brightest surface.
style_world_dna.device: A printer's device for the room: a woodcut sun with straight and flaming rays whose disc is ruled like a solar cell.
style_world_dna.imagery: Only the library's own pages and plates. No stock, no generated pictures, no photograph of Joe that we do not have.

reference_principles.source: Seventeenth-century English title pages and the Geneva Bible page
reference_principles.purpose: Composition of the home page, the reader's side-notes and the index
reference_principles.why_good: They rank a dozen pieces of information on one leaf with nothing but size, case, italics, rules and white space, and they put commentary beside the text it glosses.
reference_principles.transferable_principle: Hierarchy by typographic contrast and position; commentary lives in the margin, in a smaller italic, beside what it refers to.
reference_principles.must_not_copy: No facsimile ornament, no long-s affectation in interface text, no fake wear.
reference_principles.own_thing_plan: The margin carries machine cross-references (index names, near passages in other books) labelled honestly as machine work.

reference_principles.purpose: The chart of names that share pages
reference_principles.why_good: Star magnitude encodes importance at a glance and the sheet stays calm with hundreds of marks.
reference_principles.transferable_principle: Size-coded point marks, hairline joins, labels only where they earn their place.
reference_principles.must_not_copy: No constellation figures, no decorative cartouches.
reference_principles.own_thing_plan: Magnitude is the count of pages naming the entry; joins are shared pages; a legend says so.

reference_principles.why_good: An off-grid day is organised around the sun: gather while it is up, spend carefully after dark.
reference_principles.transferable_principle: The interface state follows the sun instead of a toggle the user must discover.
reference_principles.must_not_copy: No panel-dashboard gauges, no battery icons.
reference_principles.own_thing_plan: A small sundial control shows which light the room is in and lets the reader hold one.

signature_moments: Home opens as a book: a plate from the library as frontispiece on the left leaf, the room's title page with the sun device on the right, and a contents leaf below that doubles as navigation and as the count of what is here.
The room is lit by the reader's clock; the same page read at breakfast and after midnight is in a different light.
The reader's margin: beside each transcription, the index names on that page and the nearest passages in other books, set as side-notes.
The chart: the names of the library as an engraved star chart of shared pages.
medium_candidates: HTML and CSS with custom properties
inline SVG for the device, ornaments and chart
vanilla JavaScript modules, no build step

resource_strategy.fonts: EB Garamond and IM Fell, both SIL OFL 1.1, bundled in the app with their licence texts and served from this computer.
resource_strategy.images: The library's own scans, shown under the recorded render_pages permission and never leaving the machine.
resource_strategy.code: No third-party runtime code; the content-security policy stays at 'self'.

evidence_plan: Run the real server over the real archive; inspect home, library, reader, search, index, entry, chart, plates, research, Joe and colophon at 1440, 900 and 390 wide, in noon and night light; check console and failed requests; keyboard pass; contrast check on every palette's text pairs; API and route tests in pytest.
